radius.control: radius.2: We use a 2px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls and keep density. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough to read as an object, while it keeps straight lines that align in rows. So a dense toolbar reads as one line of actions, because the product is dense (content.q2) and precise (brand.q1), with slightly rounded controls (shape.values).

radius.element: radius.2: We use the 2px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list row or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So rows and fields read as one family, because the control corner is small, not a pill (shape.values), and the product is dense (content.q2).

radius.surface: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make touching panels read as separate objects, in a precise tone by brand convention. A small radius does this by breaking the outline at each corner, just softer than the 2px controls. So panels read apart yet still tile neatly, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is precise (brand.q1).

brand-q3.why: IBM Plex Sans for every text role and IBM Plex Mono for data: exact and quiet, so the numbers stay the hero.

items.label: Readability
items.text: Plex Sans is a neutral grotesque with open shapes, made for screens; it reads at the small body size dense rows need.

items.label: Legibility
items.text: Data, codes and IDs sit in Plex Mono, where each character holds its own fixed cell, so they read character by character.

items.label: Scalability
items.text: Plex ships a full range of weights, so every role in the type scale has its own weight without a second sans.

items.label: Numerals
items.text: Digits in Plex Mono are all one width, so columns of numbers line up.

items.label: Scripts and languages
items.text: Plex Sans covers Latin, Cyrillic and Greek; Hebrew, Arabic and other scripts come as sister families of IBM Plex, drawn to match.

items.label: Recognition
items.text: One family with a matching mono gives the product an engineered, consistent voice.

items.label: Familiarity
items.text: A grotesque reads as standard and trusted in operations tools.

items.label: Personality
items.text: Precise, as the brand answer asks, and quiet, so the brand steps back.

items.label: Performance
items.text: Two families; load only the weights the scale uses.

items.label: Licensing
items.text: SIL Open Font License: free to embed in apps and on the web.

items.label: Fallback and pairing
items.text: Falls back to system-ui and ui-monospace, as its tokens say; Plex Mono is its own pair.

For a status, use badge with a subtle fill, an icon and a word. Don't use a full-strength fill. Subtle fills let many statuses share one table.

Badge's success tone. Resolved: contained and closed.
Badge's warning tone. Escalated: needs a senior analyst soon, still containable.
Badge's danger tone. Breach confirmed: a real loss.

items.text: For the smallest clickable thing, use size.control.compact. Don't use anything smaller. Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.
Button's default size. Actions outside tables: forms, dialogs, page actions.
Button's compact size. Table rows and toolbars. Compact still fits a mouse.
Item's sm size. Long lists in a side panel, at the denser size. It still fits a mouse.
Toggle's sm size. The table toolbar, matching compact buttons. It still fits a mouse.

items.text: For a button label, use one verb from the word list. Don't use a sentence or "Please". Labels repeat on every screen; one verb reads fastest.
For the words of an error, use name the record, then the fix. Flat and specific. Don't use "Oops" or a vague apology. Experts act on the message; the record and the fix are all they need.
For a success message, use a short confirmation with the count. Don't use celebration. Confirm and get out of the way; the next task is waiting.
Alert's destructive variant. A record that was not saved or an action that failed: name the record, then the fix, with an icon.
Toast's neutral tone. A plain confirmation: Filters cleared.
Toast's success tone. A short confirmation with the count: 12 alerts exported.
Toast's danger tone. A background failure: name the record, then the fix.

voice-lands.why: Errors and empty tables are where words decide the next action.
because: What is a costly mistake? → Acting on the wrong record

items.text: For the words of an error, use name the record, then the fix. Flat and specific. Don't use "Oops" or a vague apology. Experts act on the message; the record and the fix are all they need.
For an empty state, use why it is empty and the one action that fills it. Don't use a blank table. An empty table with no words looks like an error.
Toast's danger tone. A background failure: name the record, then the fix.
Empty's default variant isn't used. No pictures: an empty table needs the reason and the one action that fills it.
